chunks: All that there is in the heavens and the earth sings the praises of God. His the sovereignty and His is the praise, and He has power over everything.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean when the Quran says everything in the heavens and earth glorifies God?
ai.summary: This verse, often cited in Shia tafsir as a bridge between divine sovereignty and creation's response, underscores that glorification (tasbih) is an inherent attribute of all existence, not merely a human ritual. It highlights the concept of 'universal submission' (tasbih al-khalq), where every entity proclaims God's unity according to its nature, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on the continuity of divine power (Qudrah) over all realms. The verse serves as a theological foundation for understanding how the material and spiritual worlds collectively affirm Allah's absolute dominion (Mulik) and praise (Hamd).
